title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, continued from p.71. Y is an analytic 'multiplicité' (an orbifold or analytic stack), possibly a simplicial or topos-theoretic generalisation. Θ is a normal-crossings divisor on Y, and Y* = Y \ Θ is the open complement. D' → Y is an immersion of codimension d that factors through Θ^{(d)}, the stratum where d branches of Θ meet. In a parenthetical NB, Grothendieck notes that what follows does not require D' to lie in the open stratum Θ^{(d)*}.

Construction. D' has a germ of 'tubular neighbourhood' V_{D',Y} in Y. Taking its trace on Y* gives a germ of analytic space V*_{D',Y}, the deleted tubular neighbourhood.

Assertion (239). There is an equivalence of fundamental groupoids Π_1 V*_{D',Y} ← Π_1 P_{D'*}, well defined up to unique isomorphism.
- P_{D'*} is presumably the punctured normal object: the (C*)^d-torsor (torus bundle) over D'* obtained from the normal line bundles of the d local branches of Θ with the coordinate hyperplanes removed.
- In modern terms: the fundamental groupoid of the punctured tubular neighbourhood of a normal-crossings stratum is canonically that of the deleted normal bundle. This is a topological form of deformation to the normal cone, i.e. specialisation of π_1 to the boundary.
- This is the basic input for describing the 'structure à l'infini' of M_{g,ν}: the local π_1 near each boundary stratum of the Deligne–Mumford compactification.

Remark. The simplest case is dim Y = 1, d = 1, D' a point. Then (239) says the punctured disc and the punctured tangent line have canonically equivalent fundamental groupoids. Grothendieck says this case looks trivial, but its canonicity needed checking. He did that in a long digression in §53 n°5 (p.758' ff) of what is evidently La Longue Marche. This is essentially the theory of tangential base points.

General case. It 'should be fairly evident' (and true in the C^∞ setting) to define the comparison via a topological, C^∞, explicitly non-analytic embedding. The next page, (240), makes this precise: an embedding V_{D',Y} ↪ N_{D',Y} into the normal bundle, compatible with the zero section and inducing the identity on normal bundles.

Caveat on the next page. Such an embedding may fail to exist for multiplicities. The example is the Z-action on E^2 by the transvection [[1,1],[0,1]] with D' = (E^1, Z): the equivariant extension T_{D'} → T_Y|D' → N does not split. The intended consequence is that the comparison is a homotopy equivalence.
errors: The transvection counterexample on the next page uses a Z-action that is not proper (it fixes the line E^1 pointwise, with infinite stabilisers). For proper multiplicities (orbifolds with finite stabilisers), averaging splits the extension and equivariant tubular neighbourhoods exist. So the obstruction concerns non-proper 'multiplicités' only; the page does not state this restriction.

The precise definition of P_{D'*} is not given on this page. If D' is not inside Θ^{(d)*} (which the NB allows), P_{D'*} must be restricted to D'* = D' ∩ Θ^{(d)*}, and the claimed equivalence needs justification there. This is a gap at the level of the notes, not necessarily an error.

ideas.what: Canonical equivalence between π_1 of the deleted tubular neighbourhood of a normal-crossings stratum and π_1 of the deleted normal (torus) bundle
ideas.modern_name: Specialisation to the normal cone / tangential base points; local fundamental group at the boundary of a normal-crossings compactification
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points, 1989); background: Grothendieck–Murre tame π_1 (1971), SGA1 XIII; Ihara, Nakamura for M_{g,n}
ideas.where_published: Ideas of this kind are in La Longue Marche (1981, circulated) and implicit in Esquisse d'un programme (1984)

ideas.what: Canonicity of the identification punctured disc ↔ punctured tangent line (case dim 1, d = 1)
ideas.where_published: Referred to as La Longue Marche §53 n°5 (p.758' ff)

ideas.what: Tubular neighbourhoods for multiplicities realised as C^∞ (non-analytic) embeddings into the normal bundle
ideas.modern_name: Tubular neighbourhood / linearisation for Lie groupoids and orbifolds
ideas.usually_credited_to: Weinstein, Zung, Crainic–Struchiner (linearisation of proper groupoids)

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates the stacky/orbifold version of 'π_1 of punctured tubular neighbourhood = π_1 of punctured normal torus bundle' as a groupoid equivalence canonical up to unique isomorphism. He flags that canonicity requires real work even in the one-dimensional case, i.e. the tangential base point issue, here dated c.1981, well before Deligne's 1989 formalisation.
missed.quote: la question de canonicité de l'équivalence m'a semblé nécessiter une vérification, et fait l'objet de la longue digression ... § 53 n° 5° (p. 758' ff)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority for tangential base points and the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,n} in Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory. Mathematically the content is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful, explicit version of tangential-base-point specialisation for normal-crossings strata in stacks, with a cross-reference to the Longue Marche. It is historically interesting but consistent with what is already known about Grothendieck's 1981 work, and the mathematics is now standard.
transcription_corrections: Line 4: the first tubular neighbourhood is V_{D',Y} (no star; a superscript was struck out). The starred germ V*_{D',Y} is the trace on Y*.
'Alors ... une équivalence' is probably 'Alors on a une équivalence de groupoïdes'.

End of page: likely reads 'il devrait être "assez évident" (et vrai (C^∞)) de définir un plongement topologique (non analytique!)', leading into (240) on the next page. 'chemins non connexes' is doubtful.
